# Integrated Sensing and Communications for 6G: How 5G-Advanced Will Shape ISAC’s Future


Learn why sensing in today’s 5G-Advanced networks is key to integrated sensing and communication in 6G


September 2026


InterDigital Comms


[6G](https://www.interdigital.com/blog?tags=6G)[ISAC](https://www.interdigital.com/blog?tags=ISAC)[Wireless](https://www.interdigital.com/blog?tags=Wireless)


*6G could turn communications infrastructure into a distributed, intelligent system that better understands the physical world. 6G’s potential depends on integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) experiments, implementations, and policy frameworks being developed in 5G-Advanced networks today.*


For decades, mobile networks have been designed to deliver communications and facilitate connection. Their next challenge is to understand the physical world through which that information moves.[Integrated sensing and communications](https://www.interdigital.com/post/understanding-integrated-sensing-and-communications-benefits-and-challenges) , or ISAC, is emerging as one of the defining capabilities of 6G. It allows networks to sense the environment around which communications are delivered. By analyzing how radio signals reflect or change as they interact with objects, a network can determine presence, movement, distance, direction, and other characteristics – even for objects not connected to the network, allows networks to sense the environment around which communications are delivered. By analyzing how radio signals reflect or change as they interact with objects, a network can determine presence, movement, distance, direction, and other characteristics – even for objects not connected to the network.


The International Telecommunication Union named[ISAC as a critical usage scenario for 6G](https://www.itu.int/en/ITU-R/study-groups/rsg5/rwp5d/imt-2030/pages/default.aspx) , alongside ubiquitous connectivity and the integration of AI and communications. Still, this capability will not magically appear once 6G networks arrive, and ISAC’s eventual commercial success will depend on upgrades to network architecture, experiments using 5G-Advanced, and more.


6G will make sensing a more deeply integrated, efficient, and scalable technology, but its future potential depends on[work](https://www.interdigital.com/wireless/5g-research)[in 5G-Advanced](https://www.interdigital.com/wireless/5g-research) being led by InterDigital and industry today. being led by InterDigital and industry today.


## **How 5G-Advanced Is Preparing ISAC for 6G**


Sensing is a capability already present throughout today’s communications ecosystem. Radar, Wi-Fi, fiber-optic systems, satellites, LiDAR, and industrial sensors already observe different parts of the physical world, but face constraints in terms of the accuracy, precision and scale 5G sensing can achieve.


InterDigital has been exploring the topic of radio frequency or RF sensing, and integrated sensing and communications, through its broader[6G research](https://www.interdigital.com/wireless/6g-research) and influence in[pre-standards and standards bodies](https://www.interdigital.com/licensing/standards) , including leadership roles within 3GPP, the ETSI ISAC Industry Specification Group, and the ATIS Next G Alliance ISAC Data Initiative. 5G-Advanced remains an integral proving ground to test and determine which signals work, what hardware must change, how sensing should be performed, and what applications will see the most benefit in 6G.


The first substantial sensing applications have begun to emerge around low-altitude aviation and drone detection, connected vehicles, industrial automation, and physical AI. Commercial activity is also kicking off before 6G native sensing is available. For example,[Orange Business’s Drone Guardian service](https://www.orange-business.com/en/press/orange-business-launches-orange-drone-guardian-europe-first-anti-drone-service-solution) uses telecom sites, sensors, and operational platforms for drone detection, and describes the architecture as one designed to incorporate RF sensing as the technology matures.


Carmakers and other industrial stakeholders are also examining sensing business models without waiting for 6G, while companies operating satellite and fiber-sensing systems are considering how their existing services could interact with terrestrial communications networks enhanced with sensing capability.


An important priority of 5G-Advanced has been establishing the ability to integrate sensing from various sources into the 5G network. The future of truly integrated sensing infrastructure is being developed for early 6G standards, today.


## **The Power of Integration**


The most consequential outcome of our sensing research may not be a single sensing application, but instead a[collaborative sensing](https://www.interdigital.com/videos/collaborative-sensing) platform through which many sensing systems can contribute trusted, interoperable, context-rich information to diverse services and applications.


For example, synthetic aperture radar satellites can observe large geographic areas and operate day or night, including through cloud cover, but their resolution, revisit time, and suitability vary by task. Fiber-optic sensing can turn existing cables into long, distributed sensors for vibration, strain, seismic activity, and infrastructure monitoring. The U.S. Geological Survey, for example, has demonstrated distributed acoustic sensing using telecommunications fiber for real-time earthquake detection. Vehicles already carry cameras, radar, LiDAR, and proximity sensors that provide essential local awareness, but their range and performance can be constrained by obstruction, weather, or line of sight. Wide-area network sensing could eventually provide an additional layer of information about conditions beyond the immediate reach of the vehicle. It would supplement rather than replace onboard sensing, particularly for safety-critical functions.


It’s important to remember that sensing technologies are not competing, but instead observing the world at different scales, positions, and under different conditions. While fiber running along a bridge may detect small deformations or patterns of traffic, RF sensing from surrounding infrastructure could provide coverage where fiber is absent, or add another observation to improve confidence. The same logic can extend to environmental, industrial, and other sites in which no individual sensing system provides a complete picture.


## **Sensing for AI**


Sensing has[exciting potential](https://www.interdigital.com/post/use-cases-for-isac-in-6g-a-look-ahead) for our intelligent 6G future. By integrating various sensing modalities, operators and service providers can generate richer, continuously updated data about network conditions *and* the physical world. This data becomes incredibly valuable for[AI-driven networks](https://www.interdigital.com/post/generative-and-agentic-ai-in-telecom) that will depend on AI models and agents to optimize performance, anticipate demand, automate operations, and deliver context-aware services. More importantly, the integration of diverse sensing modalities helps close the gap between digital decisions and physical outcomes.


When agents can plan in a digital environment, validate their assumptions against live sensor data, and adapt their actions in real time as conditions change, then the result is a powerful tool that can improve network efficiency, reliability, safety, and quality of experience while creating new commercial opportunities.


The strategic opportunity for ISAC in 6G is being fostered in 5G-Advanced today; now is a crucial opportunity for mobile networks to become a champion and integrator of RF and all sensing modalities. InterDigital is proud to be at the forefront of the innovation and industry leadership making this technology's potential possible.


Explore how[3GPP Release 20 is helping bridge 5G-Advanced and 6G](https://www.interdigital.com/white_papers/bridge-to-6g-spotlight-on-3gpp-release-20) , including the ISAC groundwork shaping future sensing capabilities.
